scenes.vo: The path of an Ethereum transaction today: First, you or your wallet send it, either to the public mempool or to a private R.P.C. (for example an M.E.V.-protection endpoint). Next, Searchers scan for opportunities (arbitrage, liquidations, backruns, sandwiches) and submit bundles. Then, Builders assemble the most profitable blocks from transactions and bundles. Also, Relays pass blocks to proposers (validators), who pick the highest-paying block (proposer-builder separation, via M.E.V.-Boost). On top of that, Order-flow auctions or M.E.V. rebates: some private RPCs and wallets let searchers bid to backrun your transaction and refund you part of the value.
scenes.cap: The path of an Ethereum transaction today: First, you / your wallet send it, either to the public mempool or to a private RPC (e.g. an MEV-protection endpoint). On top of that, Order-flow auctions / MEV rebates: some private RPCs and wallets let searchers bid to backrun your transaction and refund you part of the value.

scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. A $100,000 swap sent publicly with 1% slippage could leak up to about $1,000 to a sandwich. Sent through a protected R.P.C. with rebates: no sandwich, and if the trade creates a backrun opportunity (for example arbitrage between pools), you may receive a share of it back. Same trade, very different outcome, decided by where you send it.
